comparison: Both evaluate structural claims C57-C58. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by crystallography data, though notes the steric hindrance mechanism (C58) is inference rather than direct proof. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting better visualization of effector interference and clarification about conformational changes in switch regions.

Both address endogenous cancer cell line validation (C59-C61). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by western blot and mutation confirmation data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about long incubation times (20h) potentially causing indirect rather than direct effects, requesting short-term inhibition assays.

Both evaluate biosensor design and initial validation (C3-C4, C19-C23). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET saturation curves and western blot data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting missing optimization procedures, bleed-through characterization, and autoluminescence/autofluorescence controls.

Both address biosensor validation with controls (C24-C29). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by negative control KRASS17N, iDAb competition, and denatured variant data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting technical clarifications about optimization procedures and control characterization as part of overall biosensor validation concerns.

Both evaluate compound 3344 binding and specificity (C30-C31). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by NMR and BRET dose-response data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with significant concerns about Kd determination methodology, noting lowest concentration tested (2.5µM) is many-fold above estimated Kd, requesting alternative biophysical confirmation.

Overlapping evaluation of compound specificity claims (C32-C34). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Abd-2 negative control and multiple control BRET pairs. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation times (20h) that may cause indirect effects on signaling pathways, requesting short-term assays.

Both evaluate functional inhibition claims (C39-C41). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET and western blot data showing dose-dependent effects and pan-mutant activity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, concerned that 20h incubation times may reflect indirect rather than direct signaling effects.

Both address downstream signaling effects (C37-C38). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by western blot analysis at multiple time points. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised about the iDAb validation experiments.

Both evaluate wild-type KRAS with EGF stimulation (C43). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET and western blot data. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED with no specific concerns about these iDAb validation experiments.

Both address PI3K pathway biosensor claims (C49-C51). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET and western blot showing dose-dependent inhibition. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation time concerns potentially causing indirect effects.

Both evaluate PI3K pathway validation (C47-C48). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by consistent BRET and western blot data. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised about these validation experiments.

Both address PI3K biosensor development (C45-C46). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with justified p85α requirement and KRASS17N negative control. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning optimization procedures for full-length effector biosensors.

Both evaluate full-length RAF biosensor claims (C35-C36). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET data in Figures 2A, 2D, 2G. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting missing information about optimization procedures for full-length effector constructs.

Both address wild-type KRAS biosensor with EGF (C42). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by stimulus-induced changes detected by biosensor. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to lack of optimization procedure information for full-length constructs.

Both evaluate NRAS/HRAS biosensor extension (C53-C54). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by BRET titration and competition data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning optimization procedures for these full-length effector biosensors.

Both address pan-RAS activity claim (C55). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by appropriate controls across all three RAS family members. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning Abd-2 control molecule selection and rationale.

Both evaluate broad RAS family inhibition (C56). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED demonstrating pan-RAS inhibitor activity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to long incubation time concerns affecting interpretation.

Both address IC50 differences between systems (C64-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable interpretation of concentration effects, though notes it's inference not directly tested. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with concerns about long incubation times affecting endogenous system results.

Both evaluate IC50 interpretation (C65-C66). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as logical explanation consistent with target concentration effects, though acknowledges it's inference. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning Abd-2 control molecule selection which affects interpretation of comparative results.

Both address biosensor utility and future applications (C63, C68-C69, C71-C72). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting claims are largely speculative about future applications rather than demonstrated results. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, requesting critical missing information about optimization procedures, construct details, compound design, and control selection that prevent full evaluation of transferability.

Both evaluate background context and rationale (C62, C67, C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as these represent potential applications not demonstrated results. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging the resource paper is of great interest and not challenging foundational statements about RAS biology.

Both address background claims about RAS biology and cancer (C1-C2, C6-C9). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by established literature citations providing appropriate context. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging any foundational statements about RAS biology or study rationale.

Both evaluate RAS biology background and therapeutic context (C10-C18). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by multiple literature citations establishing rationale for cell-based assays. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging these background claims about RAS biology.
